title: Roman inherent righteousness: accepted and rewarded, not strict-law standing
source_text: XXVIII. Itaque quum dicunt homines per justitiam inhaerentem coram Deo justificari, haec non est eorum mens, Christi fidelibus talem inesse justitiam, per quam possint coram Dei tribunali subsistere, si Deus illos ad strictum legis rigorem, omni misericordia semota, examinet: aut cujus merito atque intuitu a peccatis suis absolvantur. Sed istud solum significare volunt, fideles per Christi gratiam nova & inhaerente justitia indui, quae apud Deum pro vera & syncera habetur, quamque Deus gratam & acceptam habet, & in extremo judicio regni sui gloria remuneraturus est.
pass_a_gloss: And so when they say that men are justified before God by inherent righteousness, this is not their mind, that there is in Christ's faithful such righteousness by which they can stand before God's tribunal if God examine them by the strict rigor of the law with all mercy removed: or by whose merit and regard they are absolved from their sins. But they wish to signify only this, that the faithful through Christ's grace are clothed with new and inherent righteousness, which is held before God as true and sincere, and which God holds grateful and accepted, and will remunerate in the last judgment with the glory of his kingdom.
pass_b_english: Roman justify-by-inherent-righteousness does not mean surviving strict law without mercy.
Means grace-given inherent righteousness God accepts and will reward with kingdom glory.
